chapter: Studio recordings of the late twenties and thirties
title: Roger Wolf Kahn, the rich kid who sat in
summary: Kline asks about clarinetist Roger Wolf Kahn sitting in with Rollini's group, even playing under the table to hide from his parents; Morehouse barely recalls.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Uh huh, okay. Let me mention one other thing about Adrian Rollini. Do you remember while you were playing with him, with Adrian Rollini, Roger Wolf Kahn?
Yeah.
Do you remember how he used to come by? Didn't he sit in with you sometimes?
Yes.
But he was just a kid then I think. Right?
Yeah.
Tell me about Roger. What do you remember about Roger Wolf Kahn? Do you remember anything about him? He was a rich kid.
Yeah.
And didn't he have some trouble with his parents since he was playing jazz, he wanted to play jazz?
I think he had right down in here somewhere.
Yeah. Tell me about it. You tell me about it. Do you remember how he used to sit in?
Yeah.
There is a picture of Roger Wolf Kahn in that album there. Do you remember Roger Wolf Kahn, honey?
Of course I do.
What did he play?
What did he play? Let's see here.
He played clarinet. He played clarinet. The story that I thought you might remember is he used to sit
under the table sometimes because he didn't want his parents or somebody who might know him. I thought maybe you would have known that story. I don't think he knows it.
I do remember hearing it.
And he would play underneath the table. You don't think that Chauncey remembers that story.
You know it's too bad that I couldn't have Paul Mertz here. They're coming to see me.
